complications.source_text: Diabetic retinopathy is a highly specific neurovascular complication of diabetes

complications.name: Diabetic Macular Edema
complications.source_text: At any point along this spectrum, the retina vasculature can leak fluid (and exudates) leading to diabetic macular edema (DME).

complications.name: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
complications.source_text: In response to ischemia, neovascularization can occur; this is proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

complications.name: Glaucoma
complications.source_text: Glaucoma and cataracts occur earlier and more frequently in people with diabetes.

complications.name: Cataracts

complications.name: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
complications.source_text: Diabetic neuropathies are a heterogeneous group of disorders with diverse clinical manifestations (4). The early recognition and appropriate management of neuropathy in people with diabetes is important (62). Points to be aware of include the following: 1. Diabetic neuropathy is a diagnosis of exclusion. Nondiabetic neuropathies may be present in people with diabetes and may be treatable. 2. Up to 50% of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) cases may be asymptomatic (63).

complications.name: Loss of Protective Sensation
complications.source_text: The involvement of large fibers may cause balance issues (including falls), numbness, and loss of protective sensation (LOPS).

complications.name: Diabetic Foot Ulcer
complications.source_text: DFUs can be defined as a break of the epidermis and at least part of the dermis, below the ankle, in a person with diabetes.

complications.name: Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy
complications.source_text: CAN is associated with mortality independent of other cardiovascular risk factors (68,69).

complications.name: Orthostatic Hypotension
complications.source_text: Advanced disease may be associated with resting tachycardia (>100 bpm) and orthostatic hypotension (a fall in systolic or diastolic blood pressure by >20 mmHg or >10 mmHg, respectively, upon standing without an appropriate increase in heart rate).

complications.name: Gastroparesis
complications.source_text: Gastroparesis should be suspected in individuals with erratic glycemic management or with upper gastrointestinal symptoms without another identified cause.

complications.name: Neuropathic Pain
complications.source_text: Neuropathic pain can be severe and can impact quality of life, affect sleep, limit mobility, and contribute to depression and anxiety (97).

complications.name: Peripheral Artery Disease
complications.source_text: The presence of peripheral sensory neuropathy is the single most common component cause for foot ulceration. In a multicenter trial, peripheral neuropathy was found to be a component cause in 78% of people with diabetes with ulcerations and that the triad of peripheral sensory neuropathy, minor trauma, and foot deformity was present in >63% of participants.

complications.name: Charcot Foot
complications.source_text: Special consideration should be given to individuals with neuropathy who present with a warm, swollen, red foot with or without a history of trauma and without an open ulceration. These individuals require a thorough workup for possible Charcot neuroarthropathy (140,141).

complications.name: Kidney Failure

screening_tests.name: Dilated and comprehensive eye examination
screening_tests.source_text: Adults with type 1 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist 5 years after the onset of diabetes.
screening_tests.frequency: 5 years after onset of diabetes (Type 1), at diagnosis (Type 2), annually thereafter

screening_tests.name: Retinal photography
screening_tests.source_text: Programs that use retinal photography with remote reading or the use of U.S. Food and Drug Administration–approved artificial intelligence algorithms to improve access to diabetic retinopathy screening are appropriate screening strategies for diabetic retinopathy.

screening_tests.name: 10-g monofilament testing
screening_tests.source_text: All people with diabetes should have annual 10-g monofilament testing to identify feet at risk for ulceration and amputation.
screening_tests.indication: Screening for loss of protective sensation (LOPS)

screening_tests.name: Neurological assessment
screening_tests.source_text: Assessment for distal symmetric polyneuropathy should include a careful history and assessment of either temperature or pinprick sensation (small-fiber function) and vibration sensation using a 128-Hz tuning fork (large-fiber function).

screening_tests.name: Autonomic neuropathy screening
screening_tests.source_text: Symptoms and signs of autonomic neuropathy should be assessed in people with diabetes starting at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and 5 years after the diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, and at least annually thereafter, and B.
screening_tests.frequency: At diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and 5 years after diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, and at least annually thereafter

screening_tests.name: Comprehensive foot evaluation
screening_tests.source_text: Perform a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually to identify risk factors for ulcers and amputations.
screening_tests.indication: Identify risk factors for ulcers and amputations

screening_tests.name: Vascular assessment
screening_tests.source_text: The examination should include inspection of the skin, assessment of foot deformities, neurological assessment (10-g monofilament testing or Ipswich touch test with at least one additional assessment: pinprick, temperature, or vibration), and vascular assessment, including pulses in the legs and feet.

screening_tests.name: Ankle reflexes
screening_tests.source_text: The monofilament test should be performed with at least one other neurologic assessment tool (e.g., pinprick, temperature perception, ankle reflexes, or vibratory perception with a 128-Hz tuning fork or similar device).
screening_tests.indication: Assessment for loss of protective sensation (LOPS)

screening_tests.name: Vibratory perception
screening_tests.source_text: The monofilament test should be performed with at least one other neurologic assessment tool (e.g., pinprick, temperature perception, ankle reflexes, or vibratory perception with a 128-Hz tuning fork or similar device).
screening_tests.indication: Assessment for loss of protective sensation (LOPS)

screening_tests.name: Pulse volume recording tracings
screening_tests.source_text: Individuals with abnormal pulse volume recording tracings and toe pressures <30 mmHg with foot ulcers should be referred for formal vascular evaluation and angiography.

screening_tests.name: Toe pressures
screening_tests.source_text: Individuals with abnormal pulse volume recording tracings and toe pressures <30 mmHg with foot ulcers should be referred for formal vascular evaluation and angiography.

screening_tests.name: Foot and ankle X-rays
screening_tests.source_text: Foot and ankle X-rays should be performed in all individuals presenting with the above clinical findings.

therapeutic_agents.name: Anti-VEGF agents
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Intravitreous injections of anti–vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) are a reasonable alternative to traditional panretinal laser photocoagulation for some individuals with PDR and also reduce the risk of vision loss in these individuals. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Diabetic macular edema involving the foveal center and impairing visual acuity; proliferative diabetic retinopathy

therapeutic_agents.name: Panretinal laser photocoagulation
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Panretinal laser photocoagulation therapy is indicated to reduce the risk of vision loss in individuals with high-risk PDR and, in some cases, severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: High-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy

therapeutic_agents.name: Macular focal/grid photocoagulation
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Macular focal/grid photocoagulation and intravitreal injections of corticosteroid are reasonable treatments in eyes with persistent diabetic macular edema despite previous anti-VEGF therapy or eyes that are not candidates for this first-line approach. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Persistent diabetic macular edema despite anti-VEGF therapy or when not a candidate for anti-VEGF

risk_factors.name: Chronic hyperglycemia
risk_factors.source_text: Chronic hyperglycemia is the best-established concomitant risk factor associated with microvascular complications (e.g., diabetic retinopathy and neuropathy).
